ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual-token similarity and router specialization in a base-size DiT
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 8 experts and top-2 token-choice routing on ImageNet 256 latents, and measure how far visual tokens differ from language tokens for routing: pairwise cosine similarity among patch tokens of the same layer and the change in expert assignment between adjacent noise levels. Relate these statistics to specialization through the mutual information between expert index and a 16-cluster labelling of latent patches, logged through training.
CONTROLS: A non-MoE DiT-B/2 with the same activated parameters; a router fed the timestep alone; a router with frozen random weights; FID on 10000 samples; 3 seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Patch tokens should show far higher similarity than text tokens, and the mutual information between expert and cluster should stay low for standard routers. It might fail if specialization follows the timestep rather than the content, which the adjacent-level statistic would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing statistics of an XL-size DiT across noise levels
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 with 16 experts and top-2 token-choice routing on ImageNet 256 latents, logging expert-load entropy and the Jensen-Shannon distance between usage histograms at 4 noise levels and at 3 depths of the network. Compare the final checkpoint with checkpoints saved early and in the middle of training, and report FID on 10000 samples together with precision and recall. Log the share of tokens sent to the busiest expert at all depths.
CONTROLS: A non-MoE DiT-XL/2 with the same activated parameters; a router with frozen random weights; a load-balancing loss at 3 strengths; 5 seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Load entropy should rise through training and usage histograms should differ across noise levels. It might fail if early checkpoints already route by noise level, leaving little to compare.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise-conditioned expert-choice routing for text-to-image DiTs
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 with 32 experts on CC12M captions at 256 resolution, comparing expert-choice routing with a router that receives a learned embedding of the noise level and the prompt pooled by a frozen T5-base encoder. Evaluate FID on COCO captions, CLIP score and the GenEval composition score, and log which experts fire for background and object patches using segmentation masks from a pretrained detector.
CONTROLS: Token-choice routing; expert-choice routing without conditioning; a non-MoE DiT-XL/2 at the same activated parameters; DiffMoE-style batch-level routing; 3 seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Conditioned routing should give lower FID than unconditioned expert-choice and show a clear object-versus-background split among experts. It could fail if the noise embedding dominates routing and experts specialize on timestep alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Class-aware routing studied on one benchmark with a base-size DiT
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts on ImageNet 256, comparing expert-choice routing with a router that receives a learned embedding of the noise level and the class label. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples, precision and recall, and log which experts fire for foreground and background patches using masks from a pretrained segmentation network, at 5 checkpoints and with 2 router depths, repeating the evaluation of the checkpoints on held-out sample sets.
CONTROLS: Token-choice routing; expert-choice routing without class input; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 at the same activated parameters; batch-level routing as in DiffMoE; 5 seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Label-aware routing should lower FID relative to plain expert-choice and separate foreground from background across the experts. It could fail if the class embedding alone drives the assignments and experts split by label.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-scale test of timestep versus content routing
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-S/2 with 8 experts and top-2 token-choice routing on ImageNet 128 latents, and measure what the router keys on by regressing expert assignment on two predictors: the noise level and the patch's cluster label from a 32-cluster partition of latent patches. Report the explained variance of the two predictors in all layers, plus FID on 10000 samples, at checkpoints saved through training.
CONTROLS: A router with frozen random weights; a router fed shuffled patch positions; a non-MoE DiT-S/2 at the same activated parameters; 3 seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Noise level should explain most of the assignment variance in early layers, with content becoming relevant only later. It might fail if the cluster partition is too coarse to capture the patch properties that matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router architecture comparison at small scale
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-S/2 with 8 experts on ImageNet 128 latents, CC12M latents and COCO caption latents, comparing a linear router, a 2-layer MLP router and a cosine-similarity router against learned prototypes. Report FID on 10000 samples, expert-load entropy, the router parameter count and the fraction of tokens whose top choice changes between neighbouring noise levels, using the same optimiser settings and training length for the routers.
CONTROLS: A fixed random router; a router on the timestep alone; a non-MoE DiT-S/2 at the same activated parameters; 3 seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: The MLP and cosine routers should raise load entropy relative to the linear router, with small FID differences. It could fail to separate the architectures if all three collapse to similar assignments after a few thousand steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling expert count with a specialization-promoting router loss
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 variants with 8, 16, 32 and 64 experts on ImageNet 256 with top-2 routing and a loss that penalises similarity between the mean outputs of experts on the same batch. Hold activated parameters fixed, train until FID stabilises, and report FID on 50000 samples, expert-output similarity and load balance for the 4 expert counts, to see whether gains persist as the number of experts grows.
CONTROLS: The same models without the similarity loss; a standard load-balancing loss alone; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 and a non-MoE model with matched total parameters; 5 seeds.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The loss should keep FID improving up to 32 experts, where the plain variant saturates. It could fail at 64 experts if routing collapses onto a few experts despite the penalty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the gain of expert layers persist with longer training
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts and its non-MoE twin on ImageNet 256 and on CC12M for 2 million and 7 million steps, saving checkpoints at 20 intervals and measuring FID on 50000 samples, precision and recall for the checkpoints. Fit a saturation curve to the FID gap between the two models, and log expert-load entropy and the share of tokens routed to the busiest expert.
CONTROLS: A non-MoE model with matched total parameters; expert layers with a load-balancing loss at 3 strengths; token-choice and expert-choice routing; 5 seeds.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The FID gap should shrink as the schedule lengthens but stay positive on ImageNet. It might vanish on CC12M if prompts dominate the loss, leaving routing with little to add.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatially coherent routing by region-level assignment
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts on CC12M at 256 resolution, assigning experts to 4x4 groups of neighbouring patches so that adjacent tokens share expert choices, instead of routing patches one by one. Evaluate FID on COCO captions, CLIP score, and a measure of boundary artefacts at group edges computed from the gradient energy of generated images.
CONTROLS: Per-patch top-2 routing; expert-choice routing; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 at the same activated parameters; groups of 2x2 and 8x8 patches; 3 seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Group routing should lower FID relative to per-patch routing by giving experts coherent inputs. It might fail through visible seams at group boundaries, which the gradient-energy measure would flag.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router temperature annealing on an XL-size DiT
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 with 32 experts on ImageNet 256, starting the router softmax at a high temperature and annealing it to 1 over the first 100000 steps, so that early assignments stay soft before experts commit. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples, precision and recall, expert-load entropy and the rate at which top-2 choices change between checkpoints, for 4 annealing lengths and 2 starting temperatures.
CONTROLS: A router at fixed temperature 1; a router annealed toward a hard top-2 mask; a non-MoE DiT-XL/2 at the same activated parameters; 5 seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Annealing should keep load entropy higher early on and lower FID modestly relative to a fixed temperature. It could fail to matter if assignments settle within a few thousand steps whatever the schedule.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router initialisation from features of a pretrained model
PROPOSAL: Initialise the router of DiT-B/2 with 8 experts from clustering of patch features taken from a pretrained non-MoE DiT-B/2 at its middle layer, then continue with ordinary top-2 routing on ImageNet 256. Report FID on 10000 samples at 5 checkpoints, expert-load entropy, the agreement between early assignments and the clustering, and the share of tokens that change expert during the first epoch.
CONTROLS: Random router initialisation; router initialised from timestep-only clusters; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 continued for the same steps; 5 seeds.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Clustering-based initialisation should reach a given FID in fewer steps and keep higher load entropy than random initialisation. It could fail if assignments drift away from the clusters within a few hundred steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert dropout during training as a specialization pressure
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts on ImageNet 256 where the top-1 expert of a token is masked with some probability, forcing the next expert to handle similar content, and measure the overlap of tokens received by pairs of experts. Report FID on 10000 samples, expert-load entropy and the overlap at 6 checkpoints, with weaker and stronger masking.
CONTROLS: No masking; masking at random experts rather than the top choice; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 at the same activated parameters; 3 seeds.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Masking should lower the overlap between experts and leave FID near that of the plain router. It could raise FID if masked tokens receive poor second choices early in training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shared plus routed experts for text-to-image generation
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 on CC12M at 256 resolution with 1 shared expert that sees all tokens and 16 routed experts under top-2 choice, to test whether a shared path absorbs common visual structure and lets routed experts specialize. Evaluate FID on COCO captions, CLIP score and GenEval, and measure the overlap of tokens received by pairs of routed experts, at 8 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: No shared expert, with activated parameters matched; a shared expert only; a non-MoE DiT-XL/2; token-choice and expert-choice routing; 8 seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: A shared expert should reduce the overlap between routed experts and improve FID over the variant without one. It might fail if the shared path dominates the output and the routed experts add little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing what experts compute with linear classifiers on three datasets
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts and top-2 routing on ImageNet 256, CC12M and COCO latents, then fit linear probes on expert outputs for object class, texture type and spatial frequency band. Report FID on 10000 samples, probe accuracy for the 3 labels and the number of experts whose outputs predict a label above a fixed accuracy threshold.
CONTROLS: Probes on non-MoE feed-forward outputs; probes on randomly initialised experts; a router with frozen random weights; 3 seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Probes should recover frequency band better than object class from expert outputs, which would indicate specialization on low-level properties. It could fail if probe accuracy is similar for non-MoE outputs, so experts add no new information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert load across denoising steps with a time-aware router
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 8 experts on ImageNet 256 where the router receives the noise level through adaptive normalisation, and measure how expert usage changes between high-noise and low-noise steps using the Jensen-Shannon distance between usage histograms. Evaluate FID on 10000 samples at 4 noise levels and track whether time-aware routing yields experts with distinct functions, using their effect on low-frequency and high-frequency image content.
CONTROLS: Router without time input; early-step and late-step expert partitions as in U-Net MoE work; a non-MoE DiT-B/2; token-choice routing; 5 seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Time-aware routing should produce usage histograms that differ clearly between high and low noise and yield a modest FID gain. It could fail if usage differences reflect load balancing rather than function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Position-aware routing on an XL-size DiT
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 with 32 experts on ImageNet 256 where the router receives a 2D sinusoidal embedding of the patch position, and measure how assignments depend on the place of the patch inside the image using the mutual information between expert index and a spatial cell. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples and precision and recall, with several embedding frequencies and routers that see the position at shallow and deep layers.
CONTROLS: A router without position input; a router with shuffled positions; a non-MoE DiT-XL/2 at the same activated parameters; 3 seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Position input should raise the mutual information between expert and cell while FID changes little. It might fail to help if position carries no information about content in centered object images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert capacity and token dropping in expert-choice DiTs
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-XL/2 with 64 experts on ImageNet 256 using expert-choice routing, varying the quota of tokens an expert takes at 4 levels and measuring the share of patches left unprocessed. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples, precision and recall, and examine whether dropped patches concentrate on smooth background regions according to local variance in 8x8 windows.
CONTROLS: Token-choice routing with capacity limits; expert-choice with a fixed quota of 1 token per expert slot; a non-MoE DiT-XL/2; batch-level routing as in DiffMoE; 3 seeds.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: A moderate quota should balance dropped patches and FID better than the extremes, with drops concentrated on smooth regions. It could fail if dropped patches include object edges and hurt class fidelity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Load-balancing strength against specialization on three datasets
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 with 16 experts and top-2 routing on ImageNet 256, CC12M and COCO latents, varying the weight of the load-balancing loss over a range and measuring expert specialization with the mutual information between expert index and a 32-cluster labelling of latent patches. Report FID on 10000 samples, load entropy and the mutual information for the 3 datasets.
CONTROLS: No balancing loss; auxiliary-loss-free balancing by bias adjustment; a non-MoE DiT-B/2 at the same activated parameters; 5 seeds.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Moderate balancing should maximise mutual information, with strong balancing flattening assignments toward uniform. It could fail to generalise across datasets if the best weight differs on CC12M.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Content-aware auxiliary target for router training
PROPOSAL: Add a training signal to the router of DiT-S/2 with 8 experts that predicts the patch's cluster label from a 32-cluster partition of latent patches, using ImageNet 256 latents. Evaluate FID on 10000 samples, the mutual information between expert index and cluster label, and the stability of assignments for the same patch at neighbouring noise levels.
CONTROLS: A router without the auxiliary signal; a signal built from shuffled labels; a non-MoE DiT-S/2 at the same activated parameters; 5 seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The auxiliary signal should raise mutual information between expert and cluster and improve FID slightly over the plain router. It could fail if labels from clean latents transfer poorly to noisy inputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise-level curriculum for router training
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-S/2 with 8 experts on ImageNet 128, CC12M and COCO latents, freezing the router for the early part of training and then training it only on low-noise timesteps before opening all noise levels. Evaluate FID on 10000 samples, the mutual information between expert index and a 16-cluster labelling of patches, and the fraction of tokens whose expert changes between neighbouring noise levels, for 3 freezing lengths.
CONTROLS: Joint router training from the start; router training on high-noise timesteps first; a non-MoE DiT-S/2 at the same activated parameters; 5 seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The curriculum should stabilise assignments across noise levels and raise mutual information a little. It could fail if low-noise training makes the router rely on fine detail that is absent at high noise.
